standard_prerequisites.name: Universal injectivity may be checked after an arbitrary field valued base change
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms of Spaces, label spaces-morphisms-lemma-universally-injective-local (invoked at proof line 3106)
standard_prerequisites.use: It reduces the claim to showing that for every field valued point the base change has at most one point.

standard_prerequisites.name: The vanishing situation is stable under base change by an algebra, and separation of disjoint closed subsets
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, labels lemma-vanishing-base-change (invoked at proof line 3107) and lemma-vanishing-separate-closed (invoked at proof line 3127)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first lets the argument assume that the base ring is a field; the second produces a global function separating two distinct closed points, which forces the two $k$-valued points to coincide.

standard_prerequisites.name: Points of an algebraic space over a large algebraically closed extension, and rational points as closed points
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms of Spaces, labels spaces-morphisms-lemma-large-enough (invoked at proof line 3117) and Decent Spaces, label decent-spaces-lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point (invoked at proof line 3124)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first makes $X(K) \to |X|$ surjective for a large enough algebraically closed extension, reducing the claim to singleton sets of rational points; the second makes rational points closed, so that the separating function applies to them.

core_obligations: Reduce to a base change along $A \to k$ with $k$ a field, and then to showing that $|X|$ has at most one point (proof lines 3103-3108).
Pass to a sufficiently large algebraically closed extension $K/k$ so that $X(K) \to |X|$ is surjective, reducing further to the statement that $X(k)$ is a singleton (proof lines 3110-3120).

For two rational points $x, x' \in X(k)$ use that they are closed points of $|X|$; if they were distinct they would map to distinct points of $\Spec(k)$, contradicting the separation statement of the vanishing situation (proof lines 3122-3127).
proof_roadmap: Base change to a field and reduction to one point (proof lines 3103-3108).
Enlarging the field so that rational points surject onto the space (proof lines 3110-3120).
Rational points as closed points and the contradiction (proof lines 3122-3127).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in the vanishing situation the structure morphism to the affine base is universally injective (statement lines 3096-3100). The proof reduces to a field valued base change, enlarges the field so that rational points cover the space, and then shows that two rational points cannot be distinct: they are closed points, and the separating function provided by the vanishing situation would then separate their images in the spectrum of the field, which is impossible. The reduction to rational points and the separation argument are the substance, so the claim is H2.
